summary: the reviewer and QA agents start from scripts: review-precheck lists the mechanical review leads, qa-run builds, runs the changed and baseline browser specs and checks the build output
appCreator: The reviewer starts from a list of mechanical leads (commit format, Refs, CHANGELOG, secrets, innerHTML, each pack's rules, and a public-repo leak check for mirrored apps); QA starts from one pass/fail table. New apps also get a baseline browser spec (phone width, light and dark, reload, keyboard focus) that runs in CI. This is part of #182 (item 5); item 6 remains.
notVerified: Existing apps do not get the baseline browser specs (starter files are copied only into new apps); their qa-run still works and runs the specs they have
Criteria-to-test coverage (audit A4) is not done: it needs a test naming convention in the template and planner
Whether subagents run the new scripts as written was not tried in a real agent run; the branch scenario runs the scripts directly
The mirror leak rule was unit-tested only, with no real mirrored app
